requirements.note: Inset-grouped list of all 160 recipes with a '160 recipes' header. Each row shows title, category, time ('1 hr 5 min') and star rating, with a disclosure chevron.

The Category pull-down menu lists All Categories plus all nine categories with a checkmark. Search matches titles and ingredients (e.g. 'basil' finds Creamy Tomato Salmon) and combines with the category ('Desserts · 11 recipes'). No-match state: 'Nothing in Desserts matches “choc”' with a Show All Recipes button.
Native Sort By menu: Name A to Z, Time quickest first, Rating highest first, with a checkmark. All three orders are correct, and the chosen sort survives a relaunch.

Grouped rows for time, servings, rating and category; ingredients with the quantity in its own column; numbered steps. The UIStepper scales amounts with vulgar fractions (4½, ½), stops at 1 (minus disabled), shows a 'Reset to N servings' button and the footer 'Amounts scaled from the original 2 servings'.

The heart button in the nav bar toggles (its label becomes 'Remove from Favorites'). The Favorites tab lists saved recipes with a 'Swipe left to remove' hint and a working swipe-to-Delete. Helpful empty state (heart icon, 'No Favorites Yet', explanation, Browse Recipes button).
A favorite was still there after relaunch.

tells: The category filter is hidden behind an unlabelled line-icon menu button. The button doesn't change when a filter is active, so the only sign of the filter is the small section header.
At the largest text size the ingredient quantity column keeps a wide fixed width, so names are squeezed into half the row and wrap awkwardly ('tsp / spinach', 'mush-/rooms').
The detail screen shows servings twice: a static 'Serves 2 servings' row that doesn't follow the stepper, and a separate Servings stepper row.
Blue system tint with orange stars: correct but generic. The swipe action is labelled 'Delete' when the action is removing a favorite.
A.scroll: Smooth, native-feeling list: slow drags and flings showed no blank or popping rows, the large title collapses properly, and scroll position is kept after pushing a recipe and switching tabs.

requirements.note: Plain list of all 160 recipes. Each row has a coloured SF Symbol for its category, the title, and 'Category · time · ★ rating'. A large-title subtitle reads '160 recipes · by name'.

A horizontal chip bar shows All plus all nine categories, the selected one filled orange. Search covers titles and ingredients and combines with the chip ('basil' within Desserts). No-match state with a Show All Categories button.
Native Sort By menu (Name, Time, Rating) with a checkmark. Orders are correct, the subtitle shows the current sort, and the sort survives a relaunch.

Header card with the category, the title, and time/servings/rating stats. Bulleted ingredients and numbered steps in orange circles. The stepper scales amounts with fractions (3½, 1¾, 2⅝, ⅞) and stops at 1, and the footer updates to 'Amounts scaled from the original N servings'.

The heart in the nav bar fills red when saved. The Favorites tab shows a 'N saved recipe' subtitle and a swipe action labelled 'Remove' with a broken-heart icon. Helpful empty state with a Browse Recipes button that switches tabs.
A favorite was still there after relaunch.

tells: The category chip bar is a custom control rather than a system one. Once the chosen chip scrolls out of view, nothing visible shows the active filter except the small subtitle.
At the largest text size the subtitle under the large title truncates ('160 recipes · by rati…').
The detail screen shows servings twice: the header card's static servings value and the stepper row.
The unselected Favorites tab icon is a solid black filled heart, which is heavy next to the orange-tinted selected tab.
B.scroll: Smooth and native: flings ran cleanly with no blank or popping rows, the search field stays pinned under the collapsed title, and scroll position is kept after visiting a recipe and switching tabs.

why: Both apps meet every requirement with native lists, menus, steppers, swipe actions and empty states, and neither had functional bugs. B makes the category filter visible and one tap away, gives rows category icons and a consistent accent colour, and its detail screen holds up better at the largest text size. A hides the filter behind an icon menu with no active-state indicator, and at large text its quantity column squeezes the ingredient names.
